newsitem.title: USA: Conn. high winds cause 32,000 power outages.
newsitem.headline: Conn. high winds cause 32,000 power outages.

text.p: High winds on Thursday caused 32,000 power outages around Connecticut, a Northeast Utilities spokeswoman said.
"The central part of the state has really jumped up -- it's up to 17,000 (outages)," Northeast spokeswoman Myra Humphries told Reuters.
The outages were affecting both residential and business customers and were expected to grow worse as the day went on, she said.
There were also 8,140 outages in southern Connecticut, 3,650 in the northern part of the state, 2,375 in the western part and 700 in the east, Humphries said.
"We expect the numbers to get a good bit higher before they start going down for good," she said.

"The storm is not just a front that's moving across the state. It's hanging in there. We expect the winds to be pretty much sustained into the evening. So there may be some cases where we get people back online and they're knocked out again."
"We have trees brushing into wires, limbs down on wires, trees down on wires, wires down, and maybe even poles down," she said. "It's kind of a mixed bag."
She said the utility had no way of knowing whether customers' power was out unless they phoned in to complain.
